transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-26 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Leila Gomez (CSM) — Sasha Lee (Vellum), Mark Hwang (Eng Mgr), Priya Rao (FinOps), Devon Carter (SRE), Anu Iyer (Security)
Shared artifacts: pilot proposal slide deck (https://redwood.example/decks/vellum-pilot.pdf), sample cost workbook (link), SOC2 one-pager (to be shared)

Summary:
A mid-QBR/check-in focused on balancing operational velocity (fast rollouts, low latency) against fiscal runway and model costs. Customer is running a mix of hosted Redwood API for experimental flows and Dedicated pools for user-facing inference. Main concerns: recent usage variability causing ephemeral high-cost spikes, p95 latency regressions, and an upcoming compliance audit requiring KMS/SAML proof points. Discussed pilot acceleration options, short-term cost mitigations (batching, cache TTL tuning, quantization recommendations), and a schedule for a latency stress test.

Topics covered:
- Usage patterns and recent spike analysis
- Dedicated vs hosted routing tradeoffs for peak hours
- Security/compliance checklist (KMS, SOC2, SSO)
- Proposed pilot timeline and success criteria
- Action items and next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, wanted to kick off, we got about 55 minutes, agenda's up in the deck, we'll do a quick health snapshot then jump into tradeoffs.
[00:12] Sasha (Vellum): yeah thanks Maya, appreciate it. we'll be pretty direct — last month we saw a 3x spike in inference volume around the checkout flow and costs jumped, so finance is, you know, nudging us.
[00:26] Priya (FinOps): uh-huh, yeah the billing was unexpected, we need more granularity, the token breakdown we got is coarse and it's hiding the per-route variations.
[00:34] Leila (CSM): noted; Maya and Arjun prepared a per-route cost view and some quick levers for reduction.
[00:40] Arjun (SE): quick technical note — from the trace we've seen KV-cache misses during the spike, so prefix caching could reduce tokenisation and repeated context costs, also batch windows increased CPU contention on the Dedicated pool.
[00:55] Mark (Eng): when you say batch windows, are those batch sizes tuned per-route? we're using default batching which is not ideal for our short-response flows.
[01:05] Arjun (SE): right, defaults are generic; we can set smaller continuous batching for low-latency routes and larger batch for async embedding jobs — that's where cost savings come in.
[01:20] Sasha: ok so operationally what's lower lift vs heavy lift? we need quick wins before the audit.
[01:27] Maya: quick wins: enable prefix caching for checkout, reduce cache TTL where safe, switch a couple of non-critical routes to a quantized model variant — low lift. Heavy lift: full migration of the user-facing path to Dedicated with autoscale tuning and on-prem private deployment — needs planning.
[01:45] Devon (SRE): can you clarify the Dedicated autoscale behaviour? we hit cold starts last month even though we had reserved, the burst policy didn't trigger as we expected.
[01:55] Arjun: yeah that's a config nuance; we saw threshold misalignment — Reserved capacity + burst needs the correct policy tie-in, we'll audit your autoscale rules. probably a 1-2 hour config session.
[02:07] Anu (Security): on the compliance front, we need KMS integration logs and proof of key rotation, also SSO/SAML mapping for RBAC. are those items available in the Private package?
[02:18] Leila: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and has audit logs; we'll share the SOC2 artifacts and a KMS integration note after this call.
[02:27] Priya: perfect, that'll help. also can Redwood provide an estimate of cost delta if we move the main route from hosted to Dedicated with quantized 4-bit weights?
[02:37] Arjun: we can do a modeled estimate — it depends on sequence length and token rate; if you provide a representative week of requests we can run a model and give per-100k token delta.
[02:48] Priya: okay I'll export the sample.
[02:52] Sasha: timeline — we'd like pilot to be live early September, engineering slot permitting. can Redwood support a 2-week accelerated pilot?
[02:59] Maya: yes, we can — proposed plan: week 1 configure caching/quantization and run smoke tests, week 2 run latency stress tests and iterate. success criteria to be confirmed — Sasha suggested p95 < 200ms on user route and cost < $X per 1k requests — maybe Priya can give the specific cost target.
[03:18] Priya: i'll put the threshold in the doc by Tue.
[03:22] Mark: quick concern — model fingerprinting / drift checks — if we quantize do we risk degrading outputs on corner cases? our product team is sensitive about hallucinations.
[03:33] Arjun: good point — quantization sometimes affects factuality on longer contexts; we'll run the eval harness against your prompt set. Redwood Optimize has a recommended quant profile per-model and we will share regression numbers.
[03:47] Sasha: excellent. one more on routing — during the spike some traffic came from EU and hit the US region; can we route by region to keep latencies down?
[03:58] Maya: absolutely, smart routing can pin requests by region and fall back to a compatible variant if the region is out of capacity. we'll show a config sample.
[04:07] Devon: for the stress test, i'd like to simulate ramp patterns similar to last incident — gradual ramp to 4x over 10 minutes then sustained for 20 minutes. Arjun, can you prepare the scripts?
[04:18] Arjun: yep, will do and include warmup/buffer behaviours to mimic KV-cache cold starts.
[04:24] Leila: I'll coordinate calendar invites, suggested pilot kickoff 2026-09-08 and stress test week 2026-09-13 — does that fit?
[04:33] Sasha: yes tentative works.
[04:36] Maya: ok to recap real quick — Redwood action items: share per-route cost workbook, SOC2/KMS notes, latency test plan; Vellum action items: sample request traces, billing CSV, confirm success criteria.
[04:49] Priya: i'll get billing CSV by 2026-09-02.
[04:52] Sasha: i'll sign off on criteria doc by 2026-09-01.
[04:56] Maya: Anything else on roadmap or feature requests?
[05:00] Mark: roadmap ask — we want an automated alert on p95 regressions tied to cost thresholds, e.g. auto-notify when cost per 1k increases > 15% month over month.
[05:11] Leila: noted — Redwood Console can add custom alerts; we'll scope that as a follow-up.
[05:17] Anu: small security note — for the audit we need a list of sub-processors and data residency guarantees for EU traffic.
[05:24] Maya: we'll include sub-processor list in the security pack.
[05:28] Maya: thanks everyone, i'll follow up with the deck and the action item list, Leila will send the invite.
[05:33] Sasha: thanks all, appreciate quick turnaround.

End of transcript.

Recap and explicit next steps (from call):
- Redwood to provide: per-route cost workbook, SOC2/ISO one-pager, KMS integration notes, latency stress-test plan and scripts.
- Vellum to provide: 7-day representative request traces, last 30-day billing CSV, success criteria for pilot.
- Tentative pilot kickoff: 2026-09-08; stress-test window: week of 2026-09-13.

Notes on transcription: speaker diarization has some small errors (2-3 lines), proper nouns may be mis-transcribed (e.g., KV cache sometimes shown as K-V cash).
